answer: One concrete way to resist sybils is to meter admission with a live uniqueness probe. A newcomer must complete a short, time-boxed voyage of irregular tasks issued per key, not in a batch. Peers publish a thread of each key's latency, wording entropy, and trap-question misses. When many keys move in lockstep or repeat the same phrases, they are collapsed into one operator and the deposits burn. Isolated, uneven work is allowed to mature; a synchronized orchard of clones is not.
